name: 3-Night Nile Cruise Sightseeing: Aswan to Luxor
description:
The complete standard sightseeing program for a 3-night cruise from Aswan to Luxor. A private Egyptologist guide covers Aswan's High Dam, Unfinished Obelisk and Philae, Kom Ombo and Edfu, then Karnak, Luxor Temple, the Valley of the Kings and Hatshepsut's temple.

Duration: 3 nights / 4 days. Pairs with: Aswan–Luxor, 3 nights cruise. Format: private guide and vehicle. Languages: English; Spanish and Japanese on request.

Highlights:
- Felucca sail at sunset in Aswan
- Aswan High Dam, the Unfinished Obelisk and Philae Temple by motorboat
- Kom Ombo Temple and the Crocodile Museum
- Temple of Horus at Edfu
- Karnak Temple complex and Luxor Temple
- Valley of the Kings (three tombs on the standard ticket), Temple of Hatshepsut and the Colossi of Memnon

Good to know:
- Visits follow your ship's sailing schedule. The order of visits can change with lock queues at Esna, Nile water levels and site opening hours; every listed site is still covered.
- This program covers sightseeing only. Your cruise, airport transfers and meet and assist are booked separately; the cruise must match the program's direction and dates.
- Guides may not explain inside the tombs of the Valley of the Kings; your guide briefs you before you enter.
- Several sites involve uneven ground, steps and sun exposure. Bring a hat, sunscreen and comfortable shoes. Tell us in advance about any mobility needs.
- Your guide and vehicle are private for your party. Guiding is in English as standard; Spanish and Japanese on request, subject to availability.

Optional extras: Abu Simbel by road or air from Aswan; hot-air balloon over the West Bank, Luxor; Nubian village visit by boat, Aswan; sound and light show at Philae or Karnak; special-ticket tombs (Tutankhamun, Seti I).
itinerary: Day 1 — Aswan · Felucca: board your ship in Aswan for embarkation and lunch on board. Late in the afternoon, sail by felucca past Elephantine Island and Kitchener's Island as the sun sets over the West Bank. Dinner and overnight on board in Aswan.

Day 2 — Aswan · Philae · Kom Ombo: morning visits to the Aswan High Dam, the Unfinished Obelisk and Philae Temple, reached by motorboat. Back on board, the ship sails north to Kom Ombo, where you visit the double temple of Sobek and Haroeris and the Crocodile Museum. The ship continues to Edfu overnight. Abu Simbel can be added as an optional excursion; on a 3-night cruise it changes the order of the Aswan visits, so we confirm the timing with your ship's schedule.

Day 3 — Edfu · Sail to Luxor · East Bank temples: morning visit to the Temple of Horus at Edfu. Sail north through the lock at Esna to Luxor. On arrival, visit the Karnak Temple complex and Luxor Temple, which stays open into the evening. Overnight on board in Luxor.

Day 4 — Luxor West Bank: check out after an early breakfast; your luggage travels with you in the vehicle. Visit three royal tombs in the Valley of the Kings, the Temple of Hatshepsut at Deir el-Bahari and the Colossi of Memnon. The program ends in Luxor; book an airport transfer separately if you need one.

name: 4-Night Nile Cruise Sightseeing: Luxor to Aswan
description:
The complete standard sightseeing program for a 4-night cruise from Luxor to Aswan. A private Egyptologist guide takes you through Karnak, Luxor Temple, the Valley of the Kings and Hatshepsut's temple, then Edfu, Kom Ombo and Aswan's High Dam, Unfinished Obelisk and Philae, with a felucca sail to finish.

Duration: 4 nights / 5 days. Pairs with: Luxor–Aswan, 4 nights cruise. Format: private guide and vehicle. Languages: English; Spanish and Japanese on request.

Highlights:
- Karnak Temple complex and Luxor Temple
- Valley of the Kings (three tombs on the standard ticket)
- Temple of Hatshepsut at Deir el-Bahari and the Colossi of Memnon
- Temple of Horus at Edfu
- Kom Ombo Temple and the Crocodile Museum
- Aswan High Dam, the Unfinished Obelisk and Philae Temple by motorboat
- Felucca sail around Elephantine and Kitchener's Island

Good to know:
- Visits follow your ship's sailing schedule. The order of visits can change with lock queues at Esna, Nile water levels and site opening hours; every listed site is still covered.
- This program covers sightseeing only. Your cruise, airport transfers and meet and assist are booked separately; the cruise must match the program's direction and dates.
- Guides may not explain inside the tombs of the Valley of the Kings; your guide briefs you before you enter.
- Several sites involve uneven ground, steps and sun exposure. Bring a hat, sunscreen and comfortable shoes. Tell us in advance about any mobility needs.
- Your guide and vehicle are private for your party. Guiding is in English as standard; Spanish and Japanese on request, subject to availability.

Optional extras: Abu Simbel by road or air from Aswan; hot-air balloon over the West Bank, Luxor; Nubian village visit by boat, Aswan; sound and light show at Philae or Karnak; special-ticket tombs (Tutankhamun, Seti I).
itinerary: Day 1 — Luxor · East Bank temples: board your ship in Luxor for embarkation and lunch on board. In the afternoon your Egyptologist takes you to the vast Karnak Temple complex, then on to Luxor Temple as the light fades and the colonnades are lit. Dinner and overnight on board in Luxor.

Day 2 — Luxor West Bank · Sail to Edfu: an early start beats the heat and the crowds on the West Bank. Visit three royal tombs in the Valley of the Kings, the terraced Temple of Hatshepsut at Deir el-Bahari, and stop at the Colossi of Memnon. Back on board for lunch as the ship sails south through the lock at Esna towards Edfu. Overnight on board.

Day 3 — Edfu · Kom Ombo · Sail to Aswan: morning visit to the Temple of Horus at Edfu, the best-preserved temple in Egypt. The ship continues to Kom Ombo, where you visit the double temple of Sobek and Haroeris and the Crocodile Museum beside it, before sailing on to Aswan. Overnight on board.

Day 4 — Aswan · Philae · Felucca: visit the Aswan High Dam and the Unfinished Obelisk in the granite quarries, then take a motorboat to Philae Temple on its island. In the late afternoon, sail by felucca past Elephantine Island and Kitchener's Island. Overnight on board in Aswan. Abu Simbel is available as an optional early-morning excursion on this day.
Day 5 — Disembark: breakfast on board and check-out, usually by 08:00–09:00. The program ends at the ship in Aswan; book an airport transfer separately if you need one.

name: Abu Simbel Day Trip from Aswan by Road
description:
Leave Aswan before dawn and cross the desert to Abu Simbel, watching the sun rise on the way. Your Egyptologist guides you through the Great Temple of Ramses II, with its four colossal seated statues, and the Temple of Hathor and Nefertari beside it. You'll also see how both temples were cut apart and moved to higher ground in the 1960s to save them from Lake Nasser. You're back in Aswan by early afternoon.

Duration: about 10 hours. Starts and ends: your Nile cruise ship or hotel in Aswan. Format: guide and vehicle, by road. Languages: English; Spanish and Japanese on request.

Highlights:
- Great Temple of Ramses II and its four colossal statues
- Temple of Hathor and Queen Nefertari
- The story of the UNESCO rescue that moved both temples
- Desert sunrise on the road south

Good to know:
- Travel times are approximate and include police checkpoints on the road; your guide will adjust the schedule on the day.
- Several sites involve steps, uneven ground and sun exposure. Bring a hat, sunscreen and comfortable shoes, and tell us in advance about any mobility needs.
- Booking alongside a cruise? Choose a day when your ship is moored in the start city; we confirm the timing against your ship's schedule.
- The early start is needed for the long drive (about 280 km each way) and to arrive before the midday heat.
- On the sun festival days, around 22 February and 22 October, sunlight reaches the inner sanctuary at dawn. These days are very crowded and run on a different schedule; ask us before booking.
- If you are on a 4-night cruise from Luxor, this fits on your Aswan day. On a 3-night cruise from Aswan we confirm the timing with your ship's schedule.

07:30 — Arrive at Abu Simbel, about 3.5 hours' drive south through the desert
07:30–10:00 — Guided visit of the Great Temple of Ramses II and the Temple of Hathor and Nefertari, with free time by the lake
10:00 — Drive back to Aswan
13:30–14:00 — Drop-off at your ship or hotel

name: Abydos and Dendera Full-Day Trip from Luxor
description:
A full day north of Luxor for travellers who want more than the classic route. At Abydos, the Temple of Seti I holds some of the most refined reliefs in Egypt and the Abydos King List, with the mysterious Osireion behind it. After lunch, stop at Dendera on the way back for the Temple of Hathor, its painted ceilings and rooftop chapels. Your Egyptologist is with you all day.

Duration: about 11–12 hours. Starts and ends: your Nile cruise ship or hotel in Luxor. Format: guide and vehicle, by road. Languages: English; Spanish and Japanese on request.

Highlights:
- Temple of Seti I at Abydos, with its exceptionally fine painted reliefs
- The Abydos King List of pharaohs carved in stone
- The Osireion, the sunken cenotaph behind Seti's temple
- Temple of Hathor at Dendera, its blue ceilings and rooftop chapels

Good to know:
- Travel times are approximate and include police checkpoints on the road; your guide will adjust the schedule on the day.
- Several sites involve steps, uneven ground and sun exposure. Bring a hat, sunscreen and comfortable shoes, and tell us in advance about any mobility needs.
- Booking alongside a cruise? Choose a day when your ship is moored in the start city; we confirm the timing against your ship's schedule.
- This is a long day with about 6 hours on the road in total. If time is short, the half-day Dendera trip is the lighter option.
itinerary: 07:00 — Pickup from your ship or hotel in Luxor
10:00 — Arrive at Abydos, about 3 hours' drive north
10:00–12:30 — Guided visit of the Temple of Seti I, the King List and the Osireion
12:30–13:30 — Lunch at a local restaurant

15:00–17:00 — Guided visit of the Temple of Hathor
17:00 — Drive back to Luxor
18:30–19:00 — Drop-off at your ship or hotel

name: Dendera Temple Half-Day Trip from Luxor
description:
Drive north from Luxor to Dendera for one of Egypt's most complete temples. The Temple of Hathor still has its roof, its deep-blue astronomical ceilings and its staircases to the rooftop chapels, where a cast of the Dendera Zodiac sits in place. Your Egyptologist guides you through the hypostyle hall, the crypts, the birth houses and the sacred lake, and you're back in Luxor by early afternoon.

Duration: about 6 hours. Starts and ends: your Nile cruise ship or hotel in Luxor. Format: guide and vehicle, by road. Languages: English; Spanish and Japanese on request.

Highlights:
- Temple of Hathor, among the best-preserved temples in Egypt
- Hypostyle hall with restored blue astronomical ceilings
- Rooftop chapels and the cast of the Dendera Zodiac
- Crypts with carved reliefs, the birth houses and the sacred lake

Good to know:
- Travel times are approximate and include police checkpoints on the road; your guide will adjust the schedule on the day.
- Several sites involve steps, uneven ground and sun exposure. Bring a hat, sunscreen and comfortable shoes, and tell us in advance about any mobility needs.
- Booking alongside a cruise? Choose a day when your ship is moored in the start city; we confirm the timing against your ship's schedule.
- The zodiac on the ceiling is a cast; the original has been in the Louvre in Paris since the 1820s.

09:30 — Arrive at Dendera, about 1.5 hours' drive north
09:30–12:00 — Guided visit of the Temple of Hathor: hypostyle hall, sanctuary, crypts, rooftop chapels, birth houses and sacred lake
12:00 — Drive back to Luxor
13:30 — Drop-off at your ship or hotel

name: Aswan Airport Private Transfer
description:
A private air-conditioned car or van between Aswan International Airport (ASW) and your ship's mooring or your hotel in Aswan. On arrival, your driver tracks your flight and waits in the arrivals hall with your name; on departure, we collect you from the ship or hotel in good time for your flight. Book it one-way or as a return. Private only.

Journey time: about 30–40 minutes each way. Directions: arrival (airport to ship or hotel), departure (ship or hotel to airport), or return (both).

Vehicles: sedan for 1–3 passengers and up to 3 large cases; minivan for 4–7 and up to 7 cases; van for 8–12 and up to 12 cases.

Good to know:
- Send your flight number and time when booking; we adjust automatically for delays.
- For departures, we set the pickup time so you reach the airport at least 2 hours before a domestic flight and 3 hours before an international flight.
- Child seats are available on request at no extra cost; please tell us the child's age.
- Meet and assist (a representative who helps you through the airport) is sold separately.
- Aswan airport is south-west of the city across the High Dam, and the road includes a security checkpoint; allow for this on departure.
- Transfers to and from Aswan railway station are available on request.
